edits.new: Chamomile is easiest direct-sown: scatter the fine seed on the surface of cool soil (around 55°F) and press it in without covering, since light aids germination. It sprouts in about 1 to 2 weeks and self-thins little, so thin to about 8 in. To gain time in short-season areas, start indoors about 4 to 6 weeks before the last frost and transplant while seedlings are small, because larger plants transplant poorly. Sowing in fall lets it overwinter and reseed in mild zones.
